newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: American's Crandall says fuel costs up US$300-400 mln.
newsitem.headline: American's Crandall says fuel costs up US$300-400 mln.

text.p: American Airlines' fuel costs so far this year have risen by some US$300 million to 400 million dollars due to rising jet fuel prices, the carrier's chairman, Robert Crandall told Reuters.
"Fuel is a big worry. For every one cent rise in fuel prices, our bill rises by $30 million a year," he added on Monday.
He was speaking after the first day of the International Air Transport Association's annual meeting in Geneva meeting.
Crandall said American Airlines "had done some modest hedging" and that "higher costs were always a cause for concern."
He declined to comment when asked whether the airline intended to raise passenger fares.
On November 1, American announced that it was introducing a US10 cents a kg cargo fuel surcharge on most of its international routes, but excluding trans-Pacific routes, with effect from November 15.
This followed similar action on cargo prices by major European airlines after Deustche Lufthansa AG led the way on October 25.
